properties.state: {"description":"The answer to \"what is the most pressing item?\" once the backlog lives in the graph. It is NOT detect_gaps and NOT check-health, and the distinction is the design: detect_gaps asks what the design has not yet decided, check-health asks what shape is wrong, and this asks which of the agreed things to do now. Three different questions needing three different actions, often from three different people. Composed rather than invented — BL-85 already specifies the form (\"a backlog_report / roadmap projection, a view, never a second source of truth\"), BL-68 supplies readiness and risk-to-completion (\"the roadmap is a risk-burndown schedule\"), BL-40 is the projection layer, and the long narratives stay as documents-linked artifacts rather than being crushed into properties. THE RANKING RULE THAT MATTERS MOST: an unmade decision outranks the work waiting on it. A proposed Decision with things GOVERNED_BY it is a blocker, and pointing someone at blocked work is worse than saying nothing, because it looks like progress. Measured 2026-07-24, this is not hypothetical: dec:multi-writer-architecture blocks two nodes, so the honest answer to \"what is next\" right now is a decision only the human can make, not a build task. PREREQUISITE, and the reason this cannot usefully ship first: today ZERO accepted requirements lack a satisfying capability, so \"what is unbuilt\" is unanswerable from the graph — everything accepted is allocated to something. Distinguishing allocated from delivered needs cap:derived-completion (BL-104). Until that lands, this view can rank what is undecided and what is misshapen but is blind to what is merely unfinished. PLANNED.","is_entry_point":false,"is_exit_point":false,"name":"Say what to work on next, as a projection with its reasoning shown","provenance":"authored","status":"planned","tier":"operational"}
